text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Institutional investors will be able to tender bids from March 17 for 50,000 shares in Amsterdam Exchanges. (p1)
- Health insurers collect nearly 1 billion guilders in excess premiums. (p1)
- ING group's insurance arm Nationale Nederlanden wins multi-million guilders contract from Dutch printing sector pension fund. (p1)
- Chemicals concern DSM and food company BolsWessanen opt to relocate their finance coordination centres from Belgium to the Netherlands. (p1)
- Entertainment company Endemol strengthens its sales activities by hiring Matthew Ody of U.S. TV company NBC Int. (p3)
- Aalberts Industries feels need to globalize as European markets lvel off. (p3)
- Dutch banks book 2.5 billion guilders in profit on domestic payments traffic in 1995 against a 64 million guilder loss in 1989. (p4)
- International grain and seed trader Alanheri books six-fold increase in 1996 net to 1.5 million guilders. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Cabinet to permit further growth of air traffic under strict conditions. (p1)
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo says fears Europe could disintegrate if if economic and monetary union (EMU) is postponed. (p1)
- Brewer Heineken loses U.S. market share (p2).
- Exploiter of pay-TV Nethold is to shed 100 of its 350 jobs at its international headoffice. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Recent laws designed to fight organised crime in the financial world prove inefficient. (p1)
- Cabinet vetos ingenious fiscal construction to relaunch bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker dreamt up by Rabobank RAB.CN and industrial group Begemann. (p3)
- 20 of the 90 jobs at music and film company Polygram's subsidiary DGG have to go in reorganisation. (p23)
- Legal requirement to report unusual financial transactions (MOT) ineffective in battle against money laundering, says Dutch Banks Association. (p23)
TROUW
- Environmental groups join forces to fight plans for a second national airport alongside Schiphol. (p3)
- Asset-manager Optimix forecasts the AEX-index could easily rise above the 800 mark this year. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Malaysian state company Khazanah Holding gets green light to take major stake in Fokker FOKnc.AS. (p13)
- Strikes end at activated carbon maker Norit as unions and management reach agreement on redundancy plan. (p13)
